claim_under_test: 'After he does them at least once he would learn all of those permanently, so we solve everything on a computer.' The question this round actually answered: when a demonstrated task does NOT replay, what is missing -- a description of the element, or something else?
honest_limits: AUTHORITY NONE -- one producer run in one sandbox.
The controlled A/B covers 15 tasks chosen BECAUSE the id rule could reach them, so +0.0667 is not the population effect; it is the effect on the tasks where the change can act.

The wider 130-page rerun was NOT clean: 68 of 78 tasks scored, and an apparent click-pie -0.95 was run-to-run variance, proved by the controlled A/B returning click-pie 0.05 both before and after. Run variance on this harness is large enough to fake a large per-task regression, so only paired same-seed A/Bs are admissible.
id-binding cannot help a page whose ids are unrelated to its instruction (click-pie: 0 id-bound tests, unaffected either way).
Nothing is credited: no capability, weight, terminal or family-rank claim.
laws: Before writing a module, read the module that already does it. A rebuild is not progress; it is the tree teaching the same lesson twice.

A property the instruction names is a name. If a page can distinguish an element by a property, the language must be able to bind that property to the instruction, or the page is not unlearnable -- the language is incomplete.
A high number of surviving hypotheses is not ambiguity. Ask what the PREFERRED description selects; if it selects one thing, the survivors measure redundancy.
A one-word fix that turns 0.05 into 1.00 on a page nobody could learn is worth more than a new module, and it is falsifiable in an afternoon.
Never claim a cross-cutting defect from a number whose definition you have not read.

measured_effect_kept.what_that_number_now_means: the number of descriptions still alive after one demonstration -- a measure of REDUNDANCY in the language, not of ambiguity and not of a second grammar. It must no longer be quoted as the cost of identifying a step.

replay_measurement.decision: NOT WIRED IN -- +2.7 points on 151 samples does not justify changing the preference order, and names_only_it() is shipped documented-but-unused rather than quietly changing behaviour
replay_measurement.what: descriptions learned on one instance, replayed onto four fresh ones on 12 pages

how_it_was_refuted: I wrote the 'shared language' module, then checked the existing one instead of trusting my own. demonstration_version_space_v1 ALREADY had nth, nth_from_end, nth_slot, nearest, matches(), pick() and _same_element(). My module re-implemented shipped code.
The tree already names 1415 of 1415 actionable elements: a description that selects exactly one element exists for every single one.

The 5.43 bits came from descriptions_left, which is hypotheses still ALIVE after a demonstration. Recomputed from the learner's own descriptions_of: median 42 descriptions name one element, log2 = 5.23. It is REDUNDANCY -- 42 ways to say the same thing -- not ambiguity, and not a second grammar.
Measured on the actual preference: the description the learner prefers carries 0.102 bits and selects more than one element for only 67 of 1415 (4.7%).
retraction.what_i_claimed: That acting and learning spoke two different languages, costing 5.43 bits/step in a private grammar versus 0.93 bits for a shared description, and that deleting the second language was the cheapest lever in the tree.
retraction.what_was_deleted: canonical/runtime/one_description_language_v1.py and its 11 tests. It added nothing the tree did not have. Rebuilding a shipped capability is the failure mode this project forbids.

what_was_actually_missing.the_defect: tests_true_of offered a slot-binding test -- 'this property IS what the instruction names' -- for tag, type, colour, text, full_text and value, and NEVER for id. slots_returning already knew how to cut a coordinate out of the instruction; nothing bound it to the element's id.
what_was_actually_missing.the_fix: one word added to one tuple: ("tag", "type", "colour", "id")
what_was_actually_missing.the_page_it_cost: grid-coordinate: 100 identical empty plot-points, every one tag=circle, classes=plot-point, text=''. The only distinguishing property is id='(2,-1)'. The instruction says 'Click on the grid coordinate (2,-1).' The language could see both sides and join neither.
